<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915304_theRebbe_180" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915304_theRebbe_180__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the two interpretations of "Be'er Sheva" in the verse "And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva," one referring to Avraham's Be'er Sheva (Binah) and the other to Yitzchak's Be'er Sheva (Malchus), and how Yaakov's departure relates to the refinement of sparks in the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing what is said in the discourses of our Nesi'im</t>
    <t s="2">(based on what is said in the Zohar)</t>
    <t s="3">on the verse "And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva," etc.,</t>
    <t s="4">that there are two interpretations of this,</t>
    <t s="5">the first interpretation,</t>
    <t s="6">that Be'er Sheva is the Be'er Sheva of Avraham</t>
    <t s="7">(for he called that place Be'er Sheva because there the two of them swore an oath),</t>
    <t s="8">and the second interpretation,</t>
    <t s="9">that Be'er Sheva is the Be'er Sheva of Yitzchak</t>
    <t s="10">(who called it Sheva,</t>
    <t s="11">after the seventh well).</t>
    <t s="12">And this is also the simple meaning,</t>
    <t s="13">for "And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva" was in the time of Yitzchak</t>
    <t s="14">(many years after the passing of Avraham).</t>
    <t s="15">And the difference between these two matters is,</t>
    <t s="16">that the Be'er Sheva of Avraham is Binah</t>
    <t s="17">(the Yesod of Ima).</t>
    <t s="18">For Avraham is Chochmah</t>
    <t s="19">[except that initially he was called Avram,</t>
    <t s="20">Av Ram,</t>
    <t s="21">for the Chochmah</t>
    <t s="22">(Av)</t>
    <t s="23">within him was in the aspect of intellect hidden from all thought,</t>
    <t s="24">and afterwards he was called Avraham, for he became the father of a multitude of nations,</t>
    <t s="25">for the Chochmah</t>
    <t s="26">(Av)</t>
    <t s="27">within him was drawn down in revelation even below, to the aspect of a multitude of nations],</t>
    <t s="28">and the Be'er Sheva of Avraham</t>
    <t s="29">[the place of Avraham,</t>
    <t s="30">his recipient,</t>
    <t s="31">the aspect of Sarah]</t>
    <t s="32">is Binah,</t>
    <t s="33">and it is called Be'er Sheva because it is the source that flows to the seven midos.</t>
    <t s="34">And according to this,</t>
    <t s="35">the interpretation of "And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva and went to Charan" is that he went out and was drawn from the aspect of Binah to Malchus.</t>
    <t s="36">And the Be'er Sheva of Yitzchak is Malchus.</t>
    <t s="37">For Yitzchak is Binah,</t>
    <t s="38">and the recipient of Binah is Malchus,</t>
    <t s="39">and it is called Be'er Sheva because it receives from the seven midos</t>
    <t s="40">[and it is known that Malchus is called Knesses Yisrael,</t>
    <t s="41">because it gathers within itself the aspect of the midos].</t>
    <t s="42">And according to this,</t>
    <t s="43">the interpretation of "And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva and went to Charan" refers to the going out and the drawing down to the worlds of BY"A,</t>
    <t s="44">and from there it is divided.</t>
    <t s="45">And this is also the simple meaning of the matter of the going out,</t>
    <t s="46">for "And Yaakov went out" was in order to refine the sparks that were by Lavan</t>
    <t s="47">(as related in the portion of Vayeitzei)</t>
    <t s="48">[and afterwards also the sparks that were by Eisav</t>
    <t s="49">(as related in the portion of Vayishlach)],</t>
    <t s="50">and the refinement of sparks is in the worlds of BY"A.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the name of the portion "Vayeitzei" indicates the drawing down of the Yud of the name Havayah into the aspect of "heel" (eikev) of the worlds, even to the lowest world, to make a dwelling place for Him.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is also that the name of the portion</t>
    <t s="2">[which indicates its subject and content]</t>
    <t s="3">is Vayeitzei,</t>
    <t s="4">for the entire matter of the refinements that Yaakov refined by Lavan, as explained in the portion</t>
    <t s="5">[and also what he refined by Eisav, as explained in the portion of Vayishlach,</t>
    <t s="6">which came after and in continuation of the refinements he refined by Lavan]</t>
    <t s="7">began with his going out from Be'er Sheva – the matter of Vayeitzei.</t>
    <t s="8">And this, that his going out was in such a manner that he would refine the sparks that were in Charan,</t>
    <t s="9">and his bed would be complete,</t>
    <t s="10">not like Avraham from whom Yishmael went out, and not like Yitzchak from whom Eisav went out,</t>
    <t s="11">the matter is,</t>
    <t s="12">that it is written</t>
    <t s="13">"and his hand was grasping the heel of Eisav"</t>
    <t s="14">(and therefore)</t>
    <t s="15">"and he called his name Yaakov."</t>
    <t s="16">For in the name Yaakov there are two parts:</t>
    <t s="17">Yud</t>
    <t s="18">(Yado [his hand] are the letters Yud)</t>
    <t s="19">and Eikev [heel].</t>
    <t s="20">And as explained in Torah Ohr at the beginning of our portion,</t>
    <t s="21">that Yaakov is the aspect of Yud Eikev,</t>
    <t s="22">that is, the drawing down of the aspect of Supernal Chochmah</t>
    <t s="23">[the Yud of the name Havayah]</t>
    <t s="24">into the aspect of heels.</t>
    <t s="25">And through the drawing down of the Yud into the Eikev of Yaakov</t>
    <t s="26">[and to the extent that the Yud is the beginning and head of the word Yaakov,</t>
    <t s="27">meaning that the Yud leads the Eikev],</t>
    <t s="28">behold, through this it was possible for "And Yaakov went out... and went to Charan,"</t>
    <t s="29">to draw down the Yud also into the aspect of the Eikev of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="30">even to this lowest world, below which there is no lower,</t>
    <t s="31">so that it should be a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="32">[For since the Yud of Yaakov is</t>
    <t s="33">(as above)</t>
    <t s="34">the Yud of the name Havayah, which is He was, He is, and He will be as one</t>
    <t s="35">(meaning that everything is equal before Him),</t>
    <t s="36">therefore, even as the Yud is drawn into the aspect of the Eikev of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="37">it is in its full strength.</t>
    <t s="38">And in addition to this,</t>
    <t s="39">since Havayah is from the word "mehaveh" [brings into being],</t>
    <t s="40">and the Yud within it indicates the continuity of bringing into being,</t>
    <t s="41">behold, the Yud rules and dominates all the worlds, even in their Eikev,</t>
    <t s="42">since their entire existence is the word of Havayah that brings them into being constantly from nothing to something].</t>
    <t s="43">And this is "And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva and went to Charan,"</t>
    <t s="44">that Yaakov draws down the Yud of the name Havayah also into the aspect of Charan,</t>
    <t s="45">which refers</t>
    <t s="46">[as above</t>
    <t s="47">(section 3)</t>
    <t s="48">in the second interpretation]</t>
    <t s="49">to the worlds of BY"A,</t>
    <t s="50">and within BY"A itself, the "charon af" [fierce anger] of the world,</t>
    <t s="51">this lowest world, below which there is no lower,</t>
    <t s="52">so that it should be a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower realms.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the descent of Yaakov to Charan was for the sake of an ascent, and that in order to draw down the Yud and refine the sparks, a greater power was drawn into him that he did not have in revelation beforehand.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, this descent</t>
    <t s="2">("And Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva and went to Charan")</t>
    <t s="3">is a need for the sake of an ascent.</t>
    <t s="4">And in addition to the ascent that occurred in him after and through his service in Charan</t>
    <t s="5">[for through his refining the sparks of Lavan and Eisav, he reached a level more elevated than he had beforehand,</t>
    <t s="6">and "I will return in peace to my father's house," etc.,</t>
    <t s="7">as will be explained below],</t>
    <t s="8">behold, also beforehand,</t>
    <t s="9">in order that he could draw down</t>
    <t s="10">(the Yud)</t>
    <t s="11">into the aspect of Charan and refine the sparks,</t>
    <t s="12">a more elevated power was drawn into him,</t>
    <t s="13">which he did not have initially</t>
    <t s="14">(in revelation).</t>
    <t s="15">[And in the known manner</t>
    <t s="16">(regarding Avraham, who was great among the giants</t>
    <t s="17">and the head of the Patriarchs),</t>
    <t s="18">that in order for him to be the father of a multitude of nations, to elevate the sparks that were among the nations</t>
    <t s="19">(the converts),</t>
    <t s="20">a Hei was added to him that he did not have initially].</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
